interpretation: Old auger: the white 25.5 cm x 2.8 cm cylinder with a dark end cap (x 0.25-0.278) and a collar (x ~0.413-0.426) lying along x at y=-0.0047, axis z=0.042, held in the doser's two dark C-clips (x ~0.367 and ~0.447) on the white doser plate. Perception split it into obj2 (near part), part of obj3 (plate plus far part), obj5 (collar) and obj6 (far clip). A black motor block (obj4) with a flange and a yellow gear sits 3 mm from the auger's -y side over x 0.36-0.41. Rack: the blue plate obj1 with two rows of U-cradles (x ~0.335 and ~0.465). The +y slot (y=-0.1655) held the new light-blue auger; the -y slot (centre y=-0.236, seat axis z=0.044) was empty. Goal state: the old auger lying in both cradles of the empty slot, and the new auger seated (snapped) in both doser clips at the old auger's position, collar between the motor flange and the far clip. Nothing ambiguous apart from the exact x tolerance in the slot.
plan: First plan: one top-down grasp across the end cap (closing along y, pitched 25 deg about the closing axis for reach) for all four moves, since the motor block, clips, collar and red marker leave only the auger's ends free in the doser. A lift test showed that any grip closing across the cylinder is a free hinge about the closing axis, so an end grip cannot carry the auger level. I then tried, and IK ruled out, a collar-face grasp (closing along x) and side grasps with a vertical closing axis (unreachable for the PiPER near its base). A grasp straddling the end cap and body also pivoted. A centre-of-mass grip (x~0.377, 0.13 m from the end cap) lifted the new auger nearly level. Revised plan: (1) free the old auger by lifting its far end, so it pivots on the plate edge and leaves both clips; (2) drag it toward +y away from the motor block, set it down, regrip at its centre of mass, carry it to the empty slot; (3) centre-of-mass grip on the new auger, carry it over the doser, release just above the motor block (the -y finger cannot go lower), then press to snap it in. Step (1) worked. Step (2) failed: the released old auger rolled off the visible table. Step (3) worked after several corrective presses and an x correction.

steps.what: Read robot, cameras, objects, heightmaps; measured auger, clips, motor block, marker and rack cradles from the point cloud; rendered the gripper
steps.result: Fingers about 2.8 cm wide along TCP x. In the doser only the ends of the auger are free on both sides; the empty slot is at y=-0.236 (step 0)

Top-down with yaw +90 puts joint6 at its limit, so I used yaw -90 / pitched poses. A 25 deg pitch about the closing axis gives a margin of 0.2-0.7 rad at every site. Collar-face and horizontal side grasps are unreachable

steps.why: Test whether a partial opening exists
steps.result: Treated as closed: the gripper is binary (steps 0-15)

steps.what: Pitched top-down grasp of the old auger's end cap at x=0.264, close, lift 1.5 cm
steps.why: End grip was the only free zone in the doser
steps.result: Held (meas 0.69), but the auger tilted about the far clip; the far end stayed put (steps 15-163)

steps.what: Rotated the gripper 3 deg about the closing axis while holding
steps.result: The auger did not follow: the grip is a free hinge about the closing axis. Reseated the auger (steps 163-223)

steps.what: Body grip on the new auger at x=0.30 (8 cm off-centre) and lift; then a grip on the old auger across the end-cap/body boundary and lift
steps.why: Check whether a body or two-part contact is rigid
steps.result: Both pivoted the same way; the boundary grip's gap reading equalled the end cap alone (steps 223-589)

steps.what: Centre-of-mass grip on the new auger at x~0.377 and lift 0.5 cm
steps.result: Whole auger rose nearly level; set it back (steps 589-789)

steps.what: Gripped the old auger's far segment (x~0.48) and lifted it to z~0.117
steps.why: Lever the auger out of both clips (the near end pivots on the plate edge)
steps.result: Worked: the old auger was free of both clips, tilted about 21 deg (steps 789-1018)

steps.what: Raised it to 0.15, translated to y=+0.085, lowered the far end to 2 cm above the table
steps.why: Move it away from the motor block so a centre-of-mass regrip is possible
steps.result: The auger yawed in the grip; its near end only partly followed, leaving it diagonal across the plate (steps 1018-1157)

steps.what: Released and lifted the gripper, then sampled the cloud
steps.why: Locate it for the centre-of-mass regrip
steps.result: The auger dropped and rolled across the table; the cloud caught it mid-roll at (0.20,0.16)-(0.40,0.31) (steps 1157-1198)

steps.what: Centre-of-mass grasp at the measured position
steps.why: Carry the old auger to the slot
steps.result: Closed on air (gap 0). The auger was no longer visible to either scene camera; it had rolled out of view or off the table and was not recovered (steps 1198-1359)

steps.what: Centre-of-mass grip on the new auger, lift to 0.115, carry over the doser clips, lower until the fingertips were just above the motor block (TCP z~0.084)
steps.why: Place the new auger; the -y finger cannot go below the motor top
steps.result: Held level and aligned over both clips (steps 1359-1588)

steps.why: Only way to let go without the -y finger hitting the motor
steps.result: Landed level but resting on the clip mouths, 1.7 cm above seated (steps 1588-1679)

steps.what: Closed-gripper presses on the far segment, collar, near segment, middle and far clip
steps.result: The auger see-sawed about whichever clip it rested on, so one side went in while the other popped up. Measured that the collar had shifted +1.7 cm and sat on the far clip (steps 1679-2285)

steps.what: Gripped the far segment, slid the auger -1.7 cm in x, pushed down to TCP z~0.047 while still gripping, released and retracted
steps.why: Clear the collar from the far clip and push the far part in
steps.result: Auger seated level in both clips (top 0.055-0.057 m along its length, collar at x 0.422-0.434), confirmed on left and right cameras (steps 2285-2488)

steps.why: New auger seated; the old auger was lost and about 10 min of wall clock remained
steps.result: Episode ended with the doser done and the rack's empty slot still empty

diagnosis: Half of the task failed: the old auger is not in the rack's empty slot. It was successfully levered out of the clips (far-end lift) and dragged to the doser plate's +y side, but I released it with its far end 2 cm above the bare table. A cylinder on a flat table rolls freely, and it rolled across the table and out of both scene cameras' views (images/032, 034, 035). I acted on a point cloud taken while it was still rolling, so the centre-of-mass grasp closed on air, and it was never found again. The root difficulty was the gripper physics: a grip closing across the cylinder is a free hinge about the closing axis (four tests), so only a centre-of-mass grip carries the auger level. That spot in the doser is blocked by the motor block (3 mm gap), so the old auger had to be freed and set down for a regrip, which is where it was lost. The new auger is seated in both clips (verified), but it took about 800 steps of see-saw presses because the drop placed it 1.7 cm too far +x, with the collar on the far clip. Done differently: never set the cylinder down where it can roll. Keep it on the doser plate against the clips or the motor side, or lower it all the way to rest before opening, then take two clouds to confirm it has stopped before grasping. Better still, regrip at the centre of mass on the plate while the near end still rests on the plate edge. For the new auger, check the collar's x position before pressing, and press while still gripping near a clip rather than at the ends.
lessons: Test grip rigidity right after the first grasp: lift 1 cm, then rotate the gripper a few degrees about the closing axis. Here pad contacts on a cylinder pivot freely, so a long object must be gripped at its centre of mass (found by a small test lift) or it tilts.
Use the free hinge: lifting one end of a clipped rod pivots it on the other support and can lever it out of clips. Translating the grip drags the rod, though yaw can slip.

Never release a cylinder above a flat open surface: it rolls away. Release only in a cradle, against a stop, or with it already resting, and wait for two identical clouds before acting on its position.

The PiPER cannot reach vertical or horizontal approaches low and near its base. Top-down poses pitched 15-35 deg about the closing axis reach everywhere here, and keep a cylinder horizontal because the cylinder axis lies in the pad plane.
The commanded TCP lags 4-8 mm in x (more under load), and pressing stalls about 1 cm above the commanded depth. Compensate and measure the actual pose.

When snapping a rod into two clips, align its axial position first (features like a collar must clear the clips), and push near or between the clips while still gripping; pressing at the ends see-saws it about the other clip.
The gripper command is binary: fractional values close fully.
